Allan Nathaniel Ray|website=[[FIBA]].com|access-date=January 26, 2020}} (born June 17, 1984[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3047/allan-ray Allan Ray Stats, Bio - ESPN]) is an American sports agent and former professional [[basketball]] player.{{Cite web|title=Allan Ray: A true Villanovan (Part 2)|url=https://247sports.com/college/villanova/Article/Allan-Ray-A-true-Villanovan-Part-2-164997902/|url-status=live|access-date=November 23, 2021|website=VUSports|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506224103/https://247sports.com/college/villanova/Article/Allan-Ray-A-true-Villanovan-Part-2-164997902/ |archive-date=May 6, 2021 }} He played [[college basketball]] for four years at [[Villanova University]]. He played one season ([[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]]) with the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]]. ==College career== Ray was recruited out of that year's [[New York State]] Champions, [[St. Raymond High School for Boys|St. Raymond High School]], by [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] head coach [[Jay Wright (coach)|Jay Wright]]. He committed to the Wildcats in 2001, along with three other players that made up a highly praised recruiting class. Along with [[Randy Foye]], [[Curtis Sumpter]] and Jason Fraser, Ray was part of a class proclaimed as the players to lead the Wildcats back to a championship.{{cite news|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1208/is_47_226/ai_94596662/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041129071528/http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1208/is_47_226/ai_94596662 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=November 29, 2004 |title=Freshman orientation: Jason Fraser arrived at Villanova as the centerpiece of a highly touted recruiting class, but that doesn't make the adjustment to the college game any easier |date=November 25, 2002 |work=The Sporting News |issue=47 |volume=226 |access-date=April 6, 2011}} ===Freshman and sophomore seasons=== Ray's career at Villanova was slightly hampered by injuries, but nothing that kept him from scoring 2,000 points as a Wildcat. His freshman season, he was a key contributor. He had 16 points in his Wildcat debut against [[Marquette University|Marquette]] on November 15, 2002.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170228170042/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=223190222 Marquette wins despite giving up 31 offensive boards] As a sophomore, he averaged a team-leading 17.3 points per game.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/222/year/2004/villanova-wildcats Villanova Wildcats Statistics - 2003-04] ===Junior season=== In his junior season, Ray was named second team all-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] and led the Wildcats in scoring with 16.2 ppg.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/222/year/2005/villanova-wildcats Villanova Wildcats Statistics - 2004-05] That year, he also led Villanova to the Sweet 16 of the [[2005 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2005 NCAA tournament]] where they lost to eventual national champion [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|North Carolina]] by one point.[https://web.archive.org/web/20210412221651/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=254000022 Villanova's spirited surge in closing minutes falls short] ===Senior season=== His [[2005–06 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|senior season]] was arguably Ray's best season as a college player when he averaged 18.5 ppg.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/222/year/2006/villanova-wildcats Villanova Wildcats Statistics - 2005-06] Villanova tied for the Big East regular-season championship with [[University of Connecticut|UConn]] and split their two games with the Huskies. Their final Big East regular-season record was 14–2. Overall, their record was 28–5. In 2006, Ray was named to the Big East first team, along with teammate Randy Foye, who was given the honor of [[Big East Player of the Year]]. Ray led Villanova to the Elite Eight of the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2006 NCAA tournament]], playing in a four-guard offense with Foye, [[Kyle Lowry]] and [[Mike Nardi]]. ===Eye injury=== During the 2006 [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], Ray was poked in the eye by [[Carl Krauser]] during the semifinal game against [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]]. His vision apparently left him for a period of time and his eyeball had seemed to come loose from the socket, leading most to believe it was an extremely serious injury. However, his vision returned and it turned out to be only soft tissue damage. He was able to play less than a week later in the NCAA tournament, without goggles. In his first game back, he led Villanova in scoring. While on the video it appeared as though his eye came loose from the socket, his eyelid actually went behind his eye, giving off the impression of his eye coming loose.{{cite web|url=http://ballislife.com/worst-sports-injuries-allan-ray-had-his-eye-poked-out-during-college-basketball-game/|title=Worst Sports Injuries: Allan Ray had his eye poked out during college basketball game | Ballislife.com|date=March 15, 2013 |publisher=ballislife.com|access-date=April 6, 2014}} ==Professional career== [[File:Allan Ray.jpg|thumb|180px|right|Ray during a game with the Celtics]] Ray was not selected in the [[2006 NBA draft]], surprising many Big East fans and some [[NBA]] experts. On July 6, 2006, he was signed as a free agent by the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/summerleague/press070606-allan-ray.html |title=CELTICS: Celtics Sign Allan Ray |work=Nba.com |date=February 14, 2006 |access-date=April 6, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628224044/http://www.nba.com/celtics/summerleague/press070606-allan-ray.html |archive-date=June 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} Ray was sent to the D-League [[Austin Toros]], but was recalled after just two games there. He led the Toros in scoring in both games he played for them.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press030807-recall-allan-ray.html |title=Celtics Recall Allan Ray from D-League Toros | Celtics.com - The official website of the Boston Celtics |work=Nba.com |access-date=April 6, 2011}} During the last two months of the season, Ray began receiving extended playing time with the Celtics, and had two 22-point games and three others where he scored 20, 18 and 17 points. Ray was also fourth among rookies in three-point percentage.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press072707-waive-allan-ray.html |title=Celtics Waive Allan Ray | Celtics.com - The official website of the Boston Celtics |work=Nba.com |date=July 6, 2006 |access-date=April 6, 2011}} Despite a seemingly bright future in Boston, Ray agreed to terms on a $2 million contract to play in [[Italy]], instead of having the Celtics pick up his $687,456 option.{{cite news| url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2007/07/27/ray_gets_a_raise_in_italy/ | work=The Boston Globe | title=Ray gets a raise in Italy | date=July 27, 2007}} Ray signed with the [[Euroleague]] club [[Lottomatica Virtus Roma]] on July 27, 2007.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=TFR |title=Ray, Allan - Welcome To Euroleague Basketball |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=June 17, 1984 |access-date=April 6, 2011}} Midway through the following season, after the club signed [[Brandon Jennings]] (whom Ray served as a mentor to),{{cite web|last=Forsberg |first=Chris |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4669951/former-celtic-mentored-jennings-overseas |title=Former Celtic mentored Jennings overseas - Boston Celtics Blog - ESPN Boston |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=January 2, 2010 |access-date=April 6, 2011}} Ray left to sign a contract with [[Carife Ferrara]] for the remaining part of the season. After sitting out the 2009–10 season to recover from knee surgery, Ray signed with [[Sutor Montegranaro]] for the 2010–11 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/seriea/10788/sutor_basket_signs_allan_ray.html |title=Sutor Basket signs Allan Ray | | Italy |publisher=Sportando |access-date=April 6, 2011}} In November 2011 he signed a temporary contract with [[BC Krka]] in Slovenia,[https://web.archive.org/web/20111117212214/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/89597/3735 KRKA lands Allan Ray] but in December 2011 he signed a new contract with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez]] in France.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/32743/pauorthez_tabs_allan_ray.html Pau-Orthez tabs Allan Ray] In
